quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go through the intersection. First, let any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection pass. Then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: When a bicyclist turns left:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Do not be surprised to see a bicyclist in the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch carefully and stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots on each side. Avoid staying beside them for long periods.

questions.question: You are going the speed limit when the light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop, cross the intersection carefully.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Let others go first.
No passing zone.
Fewer lanes ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let others go first.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must let other traffic go first.

questions.question: When a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are going.
Stop only if you are going the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are going.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is loading or unloading children. This applies no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a parked spot:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a big enough gap to match the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two cars to pass, then go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a big enough gap to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough so your vehicle can reach the same speed as the other cars.

questions.question: You must use low beams when:

options.text: On a lit street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these particles and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights to use with low beams.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down; curves ahead.
Slow down and do not brake.
Slow down; road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes slippery when it rains.

questions.question: On a freeway, look ahead farther than on a city street:

options.text: To see hazards early.
Because your car needs a quarter-mile to stop.
To keep up with other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes ahead. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for cars merging and changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see both directions clearly.
When the warning lights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered railroad gate. After the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: Which is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to maintain constant speed.
Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: At night, a car ahead has high beams on, blinding you. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: If the other driver does not dim their lights, do not look directly at them. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches, you should:

options.text: Pull over to the side and stop completely.
Keep driving but try to stay out of the way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side and stop completely.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights and a siren is coming, pull to the curb or side and stop. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: If you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its arm out, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are outside.
Go normal speed but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a school bus with flashing lights and the arm extended. Stay stopped until the arm pulls back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are going the same direction or coming from the opposite side.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road work ahead.
Road curves left then right.
Road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns that the road ahead will curve right, then curve left. Slow down to safely handle the curves.

questions.question: To avoid eye strain when driving at night:

options.text: Stare straight ahead.
Keep your eyes moving and scan the road.
Close your eyes for a few seconds at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving and scan the road.
questions.explanation: Eye strain happens at night. Reduce it by moving your eyes from the center to the sides of the road and from near to far ahead.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice:

options.text: Cruise control is safe to use.
Make speed and direction changes slowly and carefully.
Drive as you would in normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and direction changes slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control.

questions.question: Use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is blocking your way.
It may help prevent a collision.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when needed to avoid collisions. Do not use it to tell a slow driver to speed up or move over.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass when it is safe. There is no oncoming traffic in your way.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs always mean a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: Looking far ahead when driving on the highway:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces sudden braking or turning.
Helps you spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking ahead helps you avoid sudden stops or turns. You can drive safer, use less fuel, and help traffic move smoothly.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines separate lanes going opposite directions. You can pass when no traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams bounce off the water and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the center mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed from your direction only.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic goes opposite directions and no one can pass.

questions.question: In a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Drive a little faster.
Expect surprises.
Expect workers to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect surprises.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and workers.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a corner. Yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other vehicles turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians waiting for a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicycles, and all vehicles with a green light.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look out the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Mirrors do not show everything behind your car. Reverse slowly.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: In dark or bad weather, increase your distance from the car ahead. This gives you more time to react if you cannot see a hazard.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you. What do you do?

options.text: Move right and slow down.
Move right and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move right and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens and lights. Move to the right and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: "No passing zone" signs tell drivers:

options.text: To drive a little faster.
It is not safe to pass.
To keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: "No passing zone" signs mean you cannot pass in that area. It is not safe because you cannot see oncoming traffic clearly.

questions.question: Remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: Clear all your windows and mirrors before driving. You need to see clearly in all directions.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. Be ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before you turn.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your car when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles. Give them extra space. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: As blood alcohol level (BAC) goes up, you become:

options.text: More impaired.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: More impaired.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures alcohol in your blood. Higher BAC means you are more impaired.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped ahead loading children. You must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
Change lanes, go slowly, and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing lights and its stop arm out, you must stop. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is up. Make sure no children are crossing before you go.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. This can happen at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is standing water on the road. Below 35 mph, tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires lose grip and slide on the water like water skis.
